planning_constraints: Before provider Task dispatch, inspect the delivered F1 revision and actual reserve/settle/read/bind/extension contracts in the Feature checkout. Pin the consumed revision, schemas, refusal states and tests in the F2 plan. F1's spec describes proposed APIs; completed status alone does not establish their implementation. If delivery is unavailable, route that concrete integration prerequisite through supported supervision and finish the planning turn rather than inventing a substitute ledger or changing another worktree.

Keep one original-incident budget in the tracking-trunk executions sidecar under the Task lifecycle lock. F2 is a consumer. Carry incident, material generation, claim, operation and physical provider invocation identities separately. Preserve reservations and uncertain usage across restart; settle one invocation once. Replacement actions, provider switches and parent escalation cannot mint allowance.

Complete the provider capability matrix before dispatch: actual usage fields and overlap semantics, enforceable input/output limits, permissions and shell routes, subprocess descendants, cancellation and remote overrun limits, plus the admitted or refused recovery modes. Preserve Codex and the assigned role models/reasoning. The matrix must describe actual support rather than imply every provider supports a strict token cap.

Reserve paid turns and worst-case time before launch from planning, SWE, audit/investigation, manual/periodic and parent paths. Inventory provider shell and child-process execution as well as MCP. Each expensive route needs enforceable admission/deadline coverage or refusal of that recovery mode. Honest unavailable usage and conservative turn/time bounds remain mandatory; no invented zero usage or bill.

Prove one provider-to-production-MCP-to-real-validator journey sharing a top-level claim with separately reserved serialized nested operations. Include a competing caller that remains pending. Parent model time includes waiting for tools; process time is a separate charged dimension. Prefer one incident per provider turn; shared turns require predeclared allocation and reservations for every lineage with one physical usage receipt.

Deliver one executable vertical journey first: worker/watchdog queue, scoped owner diagnosis, real repair, Task checks/commit/delivery, immutable tested-SHA publication, then a fresh independent Watchdog postcheck of the original obligation. Script only external paid-provider/forge transports. Keep repositories, durable stores, tool adapters, validators and remote verification real; count effects independently. Acknowledgement, reported_fixed, provider completion or push cannot resolve the incident.

Use executable validation profiles with exact command, coverage, owner, approval/version, applicability and finite budget. Preserve separate Task, review and product acceptance gates. Reproduce timeout and legacy exhausted-decision recovery with retained history, permitted policy correction and authorized extension where needed. Missing policy owner/capability produces one actionable handoff or named wait; never weaker checks.

Exhaustion blocks new incident-related paid work and coalesces repeated audit/investigation requests while unrelated work remains eligible. Cover restart, duplicate dispatch, direct/manual/periodic/provider-switch entry, denied extension and independent bounded extension. Retain original failure, cumulative known/unknown use, preserved work, last material evidence, owner and next action in the one escalation.

Keep loaded-runtime/bootstrap and completed-parent cross-stage proof with F3; retain broad adversarial CI, measured budget feasibility and controlled operational evidence with F4. F2 supplies the real owner-agent seam and independent postcheck, not a claim that the whole epic is complete. No dashboard redesign, parallel scheduler or database.

Replace F2's TBD schemas/APIs and placeholder flow with concrete contracts and normal/failure/restart behavior before feature sign-off. Copy applicable diagram obligations into Task acceptance. Propose an epic amendment for any change to parent budget, authority, ownership or sequencing; do not silently amend the approved contract.

required_feature_acceptance: Replace canonical schema/API/flow placeholders through read_doc/write_doc and record decisions through record_decision. Pin the delivered F1 source revision and concrete reservation, settlement, lineage binding, read/reconcile and independently authorized extension contracts, including typed pending/refusal/unknown outcomes. If these are unavailable, route the exact delivery prerequisite through supported parent supervision; do not fabricate a parallel ledger.

Record a source-backed capability matrix before provider Task dispatch: supported provider/mode, usage fields and overlap, enforced launch deadline, shell/child-process coverage, cancellation/reaping and remote overrun limits, and explicit refused modes. Preserve assigned Codex/model/reasoning. In this checkout run_codex_role passes no per-incident timeout; run_subprocess_turn defaults to 3600 seconds and kills only the direct process; RoleResult has no usage receipt. Existing MCP scope checks alone do not establish the approved turn/process bounds.

Specify input/output schemas for incident identity, material generation, top-level claim, nested operation, physical invocation and settlement receipt. Show reserve-before-launch and exactly-once settlement through exceptions, cancellation, lost response and restart. Retain uncertain consumption; a lease clock or provider switch must not free a live claim or renew allowance. Parent model wait time and nested validator process time remain separate charged dimensions.

Assign one Task or an explicit ordered Task seam to the real provider-to-MCP-to-validator journey sharing the F1 claim, plus a competing pending caller. Trace production owner repair/check/commit/delivery and immutable leased publication to an independent Watchdog check of the original obligation. Count real effects; provider completion, acknowledgement or a push is not resolution. Include no-owner/capability refusal and exhausted-incident audit suppression while unrelated work remains eligible.
